summary.text: Moolenaar is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 2nd District, first elected in 2014. A chemist by training, he worked in business and education administration and served on the Midland City Council, in the Michigan House and in the Michigan Senate before Congress. He sits on the House Appropriations Committee and chairs the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party.

paragraphs.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in chemistry from Hope College (1983) and a master's degree in public administration from Harvard University (1989).

According to his official biography, he began his career as a chemist, then worked in business development and as a school administrator. Ballotpedia lists employment with Dow Chemical and a role as director of the Small Business Center for the Middle Michigan Development Corporation.
Served on the Midland City Council from 1997 to 2000.
Served in the Michigan House of Representatives from 2003 to 2008 and in the Michigan Senate from 2011 to 2014.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2014 and took office in 2015, representing the 4th District until the 2022 redistricting and the 2nd District since 2023.

Serves on the House Appropriations Committee, where his official biography says he is Michigan's only member; his 2025-2026 subcommittee assignments are Agriculture; Labor, Health and Human Services, Education; and National Security, Department of State.

Chairs the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party and is a member of the Congressional School Choice Caucus, according to his official biography.
According to his official biography, he and his wife, Amy, raised their family in Michigan and have six children and four grandchildren.
Ran unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary.
